clue.text: Hits making insect half confused

indicators.note: half limits the jumbling to one half of the word, and confused letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone swatting at a wasp manages only to half-stun it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' marks only the back two letters of the insect for jumbling; the front half stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: Wap is an old and dialect verb meaning to strike or throw, so waps is a synonym for hits.

clue.text: What has uncle foolishly wasted? Time

definitions.note: a noun phrase for the things a pawnbroker holds

indicators.note: acting foolishly means without sense or order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: a second is a unit of time, abbreviated S

explanation.surface: A rueful question about a relative who squandered his time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker. A wadset is a Scots mortgage or pledge, so wadsets are what a pawnbroker holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Wadsets are pledged properties, Scots law's mortgages, which is exactly what a pawnbroker keeps as security.

clue.text: Woman with fur in South American region

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: of or belonging to the pampas

parts.note: pean is a heraldic fur, black with gold spots

explanation.surface: A woman wearing fur while travelling in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Pean is a heraldic term for one of the furs used on coats of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Pampean is the adjective for the pampas, the vast grassy plains of Argentina and neighbours.

clue.text: Beats stupid people

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Scots verb, to strike or bounce
second meaning: a stot is a bullock, hence a clumsy dolt

explanation.surface: Someone thrashing a bunch of fools.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are Scots: stot as a verb for bouncing or knocking, and stot as a noun for a young bullock or a blockhead.
explanation.definitionFit: The same Scots word serves as a verb for striking and a noun for a dull, oxlike person.

clue.text: Lion, say, eating island's man of mystery?

indicators.note: something eating takes another thing inside itself

parts.note: a lion is an example of a big cat
the Indonesian island Bali, with its possessive

explanation.surface: A lion devouring something belonging to an island turns out to be enigmatic.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabalist is a student of the Kabbalah, a mystic versed in secret lore, so a man of mysteries.

clue.text: Resin spread on mica

indicators.note: spread letters are scattered about and laid out anew in a different order

explanation.surface: Instructions for coating a sheet of mica with resin.
explanation.definitionFit: Conima is a fragrant gum resin from a South American tree, used as incense.

clue.text: Cargo vessel is away, having taken heavy blow

parts.note: by can mean aside or away, as in 'put by'
a lander is a heavy blow that lands

explanation.surface: A freighter has gone missing after being struck hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A bylander is an old small Dutch-style merchant ship used for carrying goods along coasts and rivers.

clue.text: A spade maybe crushing one small creature

indicators.note: crushing something holds it tightly pressed inside

parts.note: a spade is one suit of playing card

explanation.surface: A garden spade squashing a little bug.
explanation.walkthrough: The spade turns out to be a playing card, not a garden tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An acarid is a mite or tick, a tiny arachnid.

clue.text: Pillar put atop Cambridgeshire location not long ago

parts.note: a lat is a Buddhist monumental pillar in India
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A column was recently erected above a spot in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'put atop' means the first piece is written above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Lately is an adverb meaning recently, in the near past.

clue.text: Roast set to be cut in layers

indicators.note: cutting up something breaks it apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A joint of meat ready for carving into slices.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratose is a botanical and geological adjective meaning arranged in strata, that is layered.

clue.text: Large amount said to be in these beer-containers

parts.note: tons, as in 'tons of it', is a large amount

explanation.surface: A lot of beer is reportedly held in these barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: A tun is a large cask for beer or wine.

clue.text: Explosive group a parent rebuffed

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A volatile gang whose parent was turned away.

clue.text: Small island backed by superior demigod

parts.note: an ait is a small river island

explanation.surface: A minor deity supported by a higher one on a little island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed by' means the island is followed by the superior letter, not turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitu is a Polynesian word for a demigod or spirit.

clue.text: Elated moron, frenzied devil-worshipper

indicators.note: frenzied means wild and disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An ecstatic idiot in a frenzy of satanic worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonolatry is the worship of demons, so a demonolater is one who adores devils.

clue.text: Nurses finally record twitching associated with bacteria

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of the word
an EP is an extended-play record
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Nurses note a twitch caused by an infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Septic describes a wound infected by bacteria, putrefying from microbial action.

clue.text: It's cold in regions … where such trees wouldn't grow?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: surface padding that ties the cold regions to the trees
surface padding: these tropical palms fail in the cold

explanation.surface: Cold regions are places where these trees would never grow.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis and question mark tie the wordplay to the definition: areca palms are tropical, so a cold region is just where they fail.
explanation.definitionFit: Arecas are tropical palms, including the betel-nut palm.

clue.text: Seemed to be missing a person with unreliable attendance record?

indicators.note: missing something means lacking it, so that piece is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone appeared to be absent, perhaps a habitual truant.
explanation.walkthrough: A didapper is literally the dabchick, a bird that dives and pops up again, hence figuratively someone who vanishes and reappears.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a didapper is one who keeps disappearing and turning up again, like the diving bird.

clue.text: At least twenty study on top of house

parts.note: a den is a private study
Aries is the first house of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A study sits on top of a house, perhaps twenty of them.
explanation.walkthrough: A denary is a group of ten, so more than one denary means at least twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Denaries are sets of ten, so two or more of them make twenty or more.

clue.text: Province with many people living by river

parts.note: Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: A province where many people live along a river.

clue.text: A distinguished artist, restricted going round, wearing top decoration

clue.text: Days after date in which somehow Paris no longer expanded

somehow means in some unexplained way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some days on, Paris has grown, in a way no longer seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Disprad is an obsolete past participle of dispread, meaning spread out or expanded.

clue.text: Seaman and chums, salts

explanation.surface: A sailor and his friends, all old sea dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salts' looks like sailors, fitting the seaman; here it is chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmates are chemical salts of osmic acid, compounds of the metal osmium.

clue.text: Like type of book in which poem is given new heading

indicators.note: a new heading swaps the front letter for another

explanation.surface: A book genre where a verse gets a fresh title.
explanation.walkthrough: Under the old Net Book Agreement, a non-net book could be sold below the publisher's set price.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-net describes a book not subject to a fixed retail price under the old net book system.

clue.text: Old piece of sculpture in country, base replaced with gold mounting

replaced with signals one element swapped out for another

parts.note: the bottom letter of the down word

explanation.surface: An antique statue in a land, set on a gilded plinth.
explanation.definitionFit: Statua is an obsolete word for a statue.

clue.text: Fellows backing East Anglian town, none against

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk

clue.text: Mum keeps garden tools under trees

clue.text: Tree devil cut, being without work, suffering setback

a setback pushes back, so the word runs in reverse

explanation.surface: An unemployed devil, down on his luck, gets cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: The sapota is a tropical American tree, the sapodilla, bearing edible fruit.

clue.text: Deed admitted by old man to obtain agreements

explanation.surface: A legal deed accepted by father to secure deals.

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within

explanation.surface: Someone spinning at home while hauling a box about.
explanation.walkthrough: Box is a verb here, to fight, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinar is a hypothetical rapidly rotating superdense astronomical object.

clue.text: New captain, sort who shares powers with others in group
